svg.aria-label: How to write 的: 8 strokes · 7 pen lifts · 8 movements
svg.title: Writing 的
svg.desc: 8 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 的 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 的.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E7%9A%84.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 的. Medians 1–5 draw 白: a short left-falling stroke, then the box built as 百's was — left side, joined top and right, inner bar, closing floor. Medians 6–8 draw 勺: a left-falling stroke, a long stroke down the right side that hooks left at the base, and a dot placed last inside the enclosure. Outside before inside, and the dot is the final stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, the two joined corners and seven intervening lifts; Noto's 勺 is narrower than the Arphic-derived source graphic.
